Agency: FDA (CDER for drugs; CBER for biologics)
Framework / governing regulation: Three-tier post-approval CMC change reporting (major / moderate / minor) under 21 CFR 314.70 for NDAs/ANDAs and 21 CFR 601.12 for biologics (BLAs); annual reporting under 21 CFR 314.81. Category selection guided by FDA 'Changes to an Approved NDA or ANDA' (2004), the SUPAC series, and ICH Q12. This model is the de facto regional template for North America.
Change categories: PAS=Prior Approval Supplement (major change) | CBE-30=Supplement - Changes Being Effected in 30 Days (moderate change) | CBE-0=Supplement - Changes Being Effected (moderate change, immediate) | AR=Annual Report (minor change) | CP=Comparability Protocol / ICH Q12 Established Conditions & PACMP
Notable differences: United States is the regional norm/template. Distinctive feature: it splits the 'moderate' tier into TWO notification variants - CBE-30 (30-day standstill) and CBE-0 (implement on receipt) - a granularity Canada and Mexico do not replicate. Biologics run a parallel scheme under 601.12. No true 'no-filing/record-only' minor tier: the lowest US tier (Annual Report) still requires a periodic filing, unlike Canada's Level IV. ICH Q12 established conditions and comparability protocols allow pre-negotiated down-categorization.

Agency: COFEPRIS (Comision Federal para la Proteccion contra Riesgos Sanitarios), Secretaria de Salud
Framework / governing regulation: Modificaciones a las Condiciones de Registro Sanitario (MCRS) under the Reglamento de Insumos para la Salud (RIS) and the 2022-2023 regulatory-simplification acuerdos. Since 28 Aug 2023, modifications to allopathic (farmoquimicos), herbal, homeopathic and vitamin drugs are classified as menor / moderada / mayor; biotech/biological/vaccine products and medical devices additionally use administrativa / tecnica / cesion de derechos categories. All changes are amendments to the registro sanitario (which itself is valid 5 years and renewed via prorroga).
Change categories: Menor=Modificacion menor (minor) - homoclave COFEPRIS-2022-022-011-A | Moderada=Modificacion moderada (moderate) - homoclave COFEPRIS-2022-022-012-A | Mayor=Modificacion mayor (major) - homoclave COFEPRIS-2022-022-013-A | Prorroga=Prorroga del registro sanitario (registration renewal)
Notable differences: Mexico diverges most from the US/Canada regional norm. (1) It is registration-centric: every CMC change is an amendment to the registro sanitario (a 5-year, renewable license) rather than a supplement to a marketing application. (2) Its three-tier menor/moderada/mayor scheme (introduced 2023) is risk-graded like the US but there is NO record-only/no-filing tier - even minor changes require a COFEPRIS constancia. (3) Unique 'Ventanilla de Resolucion Inmediata' issues same-day authorizations for minor and moderate changes, compressing prior approval into an immediate transaction rather than offering a true notification-only path. (4) Uses homoclave-coded tramites and Spanish-language dossiers; biologics/vaccines and devices carry additional administrativa/tecnica/cesion-de-derechos subcategories.

Agency: ANVISA (Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária)
Framework / governing regulation: Post-approval CMC changes are governed by two parallel tiered regimes: RDC 73/2016 for synthetic and semi-synthetic drugs, and RDC 913/2024 for biological products (which revoked RDC 413/2020). Both classify changes by potential impact on quality/safety/efficacy into (a) immediate-implementation changes (implement on protocol/HMP entry, subject to later ANVISA review) and (b) prior-approval changes. RDC 219/2018 adds 'conditional approval': ANVISA silence within the statutory clock is deemed approval (deferimento tácito). This is the most granular and reliance-forward regime in LATAM.
Change categories: SIN-II=Synthetic drug: immediate-implementation change (mudança de implementação imediata, Anexo I RDC 73/2016) | SIN-AP=Synthetic drug: prior-approval change (mudança sujeita a aprovação prévia) | SIN-NOT-BULA=Synthetic drug: labeling/leaflet (bula) notification | BIO-MAJOR=Biological product: major quality change (RDC 913/2024) | BIO-MODERATE=Biological product: moderate quality change (RDC 913/2024) | BIO-MINOR=Biological product: minor change (RDC 913/2024) | BIO-SAFEFF=Biological product: efficacy/safety change (RDC 913/2024)
Notable differences: Brazil is the LATAM outlier in sophistication: it is the closest to an EU-style tiered system with a genuine immediate-implementation (implement-then-report) tier plus conditional/tacit approval (RDC 219/2018), whereas most of the region is prior-approval-dominant. Separate, fully articulated regimes exist for synthetic (RDC 73/2016) vs biologics (RDC 913/2024, replacing RDC 413/2020). Uses local 'assunto' subject codes and a mandatory PATE technical opinion.

Agency: ANMAT (Administración Nacional de Medicamentos, Alimentos y Tecnología Médica)
Framework / governing regulation: Post-approval modifications ('modificaciones post-registro') to a marketing authorization are set by ANMAT Disposiciones. Historically a two-tier system: modifications requiring prior authorization vs. those subject to notification: administered through the traditional registration Disposiciones (e.g., Disp. 5755/1996 for synthetics and later amendments). For biologicals, a new risk-based framework was adopted in 2026: Disposición 4351/2026, which classifies modifications (quality, safety, efficacy, labeling, and authorization extensions) by risk into distinct procedures with maximum statutory resolution timeframes, and formally introduces reliance on high-vigilance foreign agencies (FDA/EMA).
Change categories: AR-MOD-AUT=Modification requiring prior authorization (autorización previa) | AR-MOD-NOTIF=Modification subject to notification (menor impacto) | AR-BIO-RISK=Biological product: risk-classified modification (Disp. 4351/2026)
Notable differences: Argentina is mid-reform. The synthetic-drug post-registration regime remains the traditional prior-authorization vs. notification split under legacy Disposiciones, while biologicals moved (2026) to an explicitly risk-based, reliance-enabled system (Disp. 4351/2026) aligning with FDA/EMA: a stronger, more formalized reliance stance than most LATAM peers. No EU-style IA/IB/II lettering.

Agency: European Commission / European Medicines Agency (EMA) for centrally authorised products; national competent authorities (NCAs) via CMDh for MRP/DCP/national products
Framework / governing regulation: Harmonized EU variations framework: Type IA / IA_IN / IB / II / Extension under Commission Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008 as amended by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1701 (applicable 1 Jan 2025), with classification/documentation detailed in Commission Guideline C/2025/5045 (applicable 15 Jan 2026, superseding Guideline 2013/C 223/01). Applies uniformly across all 27 EU member states plus the EEA (Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein) via the EEA Agreement, through the CP, MRP, DCP and purely national procedures.
Change categories: IA=Minor variation Type IA (Do-and-Document / annual grouping) | IA_IN=Minor variation Type IA requiring Immediate Notification | IB=Minor variation Type IB (default 'tell-wait') | II=Major variation Type II (prior approval) | EXT=Extension of the marketing authorisation
Notable differences: This is the regional norm. The 2024/1701 reform (applicable 1 Jan 2025) plus Guideline C/2025/5045 (applicable 15 Jan 2026) are the two structural changes vs the historic 2013/C 223/01 baseline: (1) standard Type IA variations can no longer be filed individually and must be bundled into an annual Type IA grouping ('annual update'); (2) worksharing is mandatory when an identical change including ≥1 Type IB/II variation affects multiple MAs of the same holder; (3) optional PACMP and PLCM tools are formalised. Scope is now limited to human medicinal products.

Agency: National competent authority (+ EMA for centrally authorised products)
Framework / governing regulation: Same harmonized categories (Type IA / IA_IN / IB / II / Extension) under Reg (EC) 1234/2008 as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/1701 and Guideline C/2025/5045. Directly applicable in all 27 member states; the three EEA-EFTA states (Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein) incorporate the EU pharmaceutical acquis via the EEA Agreement so the same variation categories and procedures apply.
Change categories: IA=Minor variation Type IA (annual update / do-and-document) | IA_IN=Minor variation Type IA: immediate notification | IB=Minor variation Type IB (tell-wait, default) | II=Major variation Type II (prior approval) | EXT=Extension of the MA
Notable differences: Harmonized under Reg (EC) 1234/2008 as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/1701; classification Guideline C/2025/5045 (from 15 Jan 2026). Same categories (IA/IA_IN/IB/II/Extension) via Centralised/MRP/DCP; purely national MAs follow national variation rules transposing the Regulation.

Agency: National competent authority (+ EMA for centrally authorised products)
Framework / governing regulation: Same harmonized categories (Type IA / IA_IN / IB / II / Extension) under Reg (EC) 1234/2008 as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/1701 and Guideline C/2025/5045. Directly applicable in all 27 member states; the three EEA-EFTA states (Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein) incorporate the EU pharmaceutical acquis via the EEA Agreement so the same variation categories and procedures apply.
Change categories: IA=Minor variation Type IA (annual update / do-and-document) | IA_IN=Minor variation Type IA: immediate notification | IB=Minor variation Type IB (tell-wait, default) | II=Major variation Type II (prior approval) | EXT=Extension of the MA
Notable differences: Harmonized under Reg (EC) 1234/2008 as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/1701; classification Guideline C/2025/5045 (from 15 Jan 2026). Same categories (IA/IA_IN/IB/II/Extension) via Centralised/MRP/DCP; purely national MAs follow national variation rules transposing the Regulation.

Agency: National competent authority (EEA; EU acquis via EEA Agreement)
Framework / governing regulation: Same harmonized categories (Type IA / IA_IN / IB / II / Extension) under Reg (EC) 1234/2008 as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/1701 and Guideline C/2025/5045. Directly applicable in all 27 member states; the three EEA-EFTA states (Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein) incorporate the EU pharmaceutical acquis via the EEA Agreement so the same variation categories and procedures apply.
Change categories: IA=Minor variation Type IA (annual update / do-and-document) | IA_IN=Minor variation Type IA: immediate notification | IB=Minor variation Type IB (tell-wait, default) | II=Major variation Type II (prior approval) | EXT=Extension of the MA
Notable differences: Harmonized under Reg (EC) 1234/2008 as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/1701; classification Guideline C/2025/5045 (from 15 Jan 2026). Same categories (IA/IA_IN/IB/II/Extension) via Centralised/MRP/DCP; purely national MAs follow national variation rules transposing the Regulation. EEA state applies the EU variations acquis via the EEA Agreement.

Agency: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA)
Framework / governing regulation: UK national variations regime under the Human Medicines Regulations 2012 (SI 2012/1916), Regulation 65C and Schedule 10A, which retained the pre-Brexit Chapter IIa procedures of Reg (EC) 1234/2008 as they stood at end of the transition period. Categories remain Type IA / IA_IN / IB / II / Extension, and the EU 2013 classification guideline continues to apply until MHRA issues revised national guidance.
Change categories: IA=Minor variation Type IA (do-and-tell) | IA_IN=Minor variation Type IA: immediate notification | IB=Minor variation Type IB (tell-wait) | II=Major variation Type II (prior approval) | EXT=Extension of the MA
Notable differences: DIVERGES from the current EU norm: the UK retained the pre-reform (2013) EU classification framework and has NOT adopted Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1701. Consequently the UK does not impose the EU's mandatory annual Type IA grouping or mandatory worksharing; Type IA notifications retain the classic 'within 12 months' individual/grouped option. UK MAs are purely national (single MHRA assessment, no RMS/CMS); the Windsor Framework (from 1 Jan 2025) governs the Northern Ireland/GB interface. MHRA has signalled it may issue its own revised guidance but the EU 2013 classification continues to apply in the interim.

Agency: Swissmedic (Swiss Agency for Therapeutic Products)
Framework / governing regulation: Swiss national regime under the Therapeutic Products Act (HMG/LPTh) and the Ordinance on Medicinal Products (VAM/OAMéd), operationalised in Swissmedic guidance document ZL300 (Variations and extensions for human medicinal products). Uses variation categories aligned in structure to the EU: minor variations reported subsequently (Type IA/IA_IN), minor variations reported in advance (Type IB), major variations (Type II), and extensions: and references the EU classification guideline for categorisation.
Change categories: IA=Minor variation to be reported subsequently (Type IA/IA_IN) | IB=Minor variation to be reported in advance (Type IB) | II=Major variation (Type II) | EXT=Extension of the authorisation
Notable differences: DIFFERS from the EU norm as a non-EU/non-EEA country: Switzerland regulates independently under the Therapeutic Products Act and the Ordinance on Medicinal Products, with Swissmedic as sole authority (no CP/MRP/DCP, no RMS/CMS). It mirrors the EU category STRUCTURE (IA/IA_IN reported subsequently, IB reported in advance, II, extension) and references the EU classification guideline (ZL300 updated Feb 2026 to reflect the updated EU guideline), but timelines, fees, submission format and the legal basis are Swiss-specific rather than Reg 1234/2008. Not bound by Reg (EU) 2024/1701; Liechtenstein recognises Swiss authorisations under the CH-LI customs union.

Agency: National Medical Products Administration (NMPA); provincial Medical Products Administrations (record-filings)
Framework / governing regulation: Risk-based three-tier post-approval change system under the Provisions for Drug Registration (Order No. 27, 2020, effective 1 Jul 2020) and NMPA post-approval change management announcements/technical guidelines: major = supplemental application (补充申请, approval); moderate = record-filing (备案, filing); minor = annual report (年度报告). Note the 2026 Implementing Regulations of the Drug Administration Law are reshaping the broader framework.
Change categories: SUPP=Supplemental Application (补充申请) | REC=Record-Filing / Bei'an (备案) | AR=Annual Report (年度报告)
Notable differences: Closely mirrors the regional risk-based three-tier norm (approval / filing / annual report), most similar to Canada's four-level and EU's IA/IB/II gradient. Distinctive: the moderate 'record-filing' (备案) tier is handled at the PROVINCIAL MPA level (not central NMPA), and the MAH self-classifies against NMPA technical guidelines with retrospective authority review. The framework is in flux under the 2026 Implementing Regulations of the Drug Administration Law.

Region: ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations): 11 member states
Agency: Health Sciences Authority (HSA), Health Products Regulation Group
Framework / governing regulation: Variation of a registered therapeutic product under the Health Products Act 2007 and Health Products (Therapeutic Products) Regulations 2016. HSA's own tiered scheme (MAV / MIV) is broadly aligned to the ASEAN Variation Guideline but is the most granular in the region, splitting minor variations into prior-approval, notification-with-standstill, and do-and-tell, plus a list of non-notifiable changes. Details in the Guidance on Therapeutic Product Registration in Singapore (Appendices 13/14 for MIV, Appendix 5 for target processing timelines).
Change categories: MAV-1 / MAV-2=Major Variation Application | MIV-1=Minor Variation Application (prior approval) | MIV-2 (Notification)=Minor Variation: Notification (standstill) | MIV-2 (Do-and-Tell)=Minor Variation: Do-and-Tell | Non-notifiable=Changes not requiring notification to HSA
Notable differences: Most granular scheme in ASEAN. Uniquely splits the notification tier into a 40-working-day standstill notification (MIV-2 Notification: notify-then-wait) and a true do-and-tell (MIV-2 Do-and-Tell, submit within 6 months), and publishes an explicit no-filing list. Uses PRISM e-submission and abridged/verification reliance routes with target working-day timelines and stop-clocks: more transparent and codified than the AVG's 'country-specific' placeholders.

Region: ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations): 11 member states
Agency: National Pharmaceutical Regulatory Agency (NPRA), Drug Control Authority (DCA)
Framework / governing regulation: Variations to a registered pharmaceutical product under the Control of Drugs and Cosmetics Regulations 1984. Direct national implementation of the ASEAN Variation Guideline via the Malaysian Variation Guideline for Pharmaceutical Products (2nd Edition / Revision 1, July 2022) and the Drug Registration Guidance Document (DRGD). Three tiers: MaV, MiV-PA, MiV-N, processed through the QUEST online system.
Change categories: MaV=Major Variation | MiV-PA=Minor Variation: Prior Approval | MiV-PA* (Tell & Do)=Minor Variation: Prior Approval eligible for Tell & Do | MiV-N=Minor Variation: Notification (Do & Tell)
Notable differences: Faithful AVG implementer but extends it: (a) an explicit MiV-PA* 'Tell & Do' subset that may be implemented at submission; (b) more MiV-PA/MiV-N sub-codes than the base AVG; (c) codified working-day acknowledgment (MiV-N 30 wd) and implementation windows (MaV/MiV-PA within 6 months of approval; MiV-N up to 12 months after implementation) via the QUEST system. Biologics handled under separate NPRA/DRGD provisions (AVG excludes biologics).

Region: ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations): 11 member states
Agency: Thai Food and Drug Administration (Thai FDA), Bureau of Drug Control, Ministry of Public Health
Framework / governing regulation: Variations to a drug registration under the Drug Act B.E. 2510 (1967) and Ministerial Regulation No. 18 (B.E. 2525). Thai FDA has adopted the ASEAN harmonised framework (ACTD/ACTR and the ASEAN Variation Guideline), classifying post-approval changes as MaV / MiV-PA / MiV-N with eCTD submission.
Change categories: MaV=Major Variation | MiV-PA=Minor Variation: Prior Approval | MiV-N=Minor Variation: Notification (Do & Tell)
Notable differences: Implements the ASEAN MaV/MiV-PA/MiV-N tiers largely unchanged, tied to the Drug Act B.E. 2510 and Ministerial Regulation No. 18. Category-specific working-day clocks are less transparently published in English than Singapore/Malaysia; the AVG's 'country-specific proposal' placeholders are set by Thai FDA internal SLAs.

Region: ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations): 11 member states
Agency: Badan Pengawas Obat dan Makanan (BPOM): National Agency of Drug and Food Control
Framework / governing regulation: Registrasi Variasi Obat (drug variation registration) under BPOM Regulation No. 24 of 2017 on Criteria and Procedures for Drug Registration, as amended (incl. PerBPOM 13/2021 3rd amendment; PerBPOM 15/2023 4th amendment; PerBPOM 23/2025 5th amendment). Three tiers aligned to the ASEAN model: Variasi Major, Variasi Minor, Variasi Notifikasi, submitted via the New-AERO online system.
Change categories: Variasi Major=Major Variation (Registrasi Variasi Major) | Variasi Minor=Minor Variation (Registrasi Variasi Minor) | Variasi Notifikasi=Notification Variation (Registrasi Variasi Notifikasi)
Notable differences: Three-tier Major/Minor/Notifikasi maps cleanly to AVG MaV/MiV-PA/MiV-N but is embedded in a national registration decree (PerBPOM 24/2017 and its five amendments) rather than a standalone variation guideline, and is administered in Bahasa Indonesia via New-AERO. Timelines are counted in working days ('hari kerja').

Region: ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations): 11 member states
Agency: Food and Drug Administration (FDA Philippines), Center for Drug Regulation and Research (CDRR)
Framework / governing regulation: Post-approval changes to registered pharmaceutical products under RA 9711 (FDA Act of 2009) and its IRR, AO No. 2024-0013, and the current FDA Circular on Implementing Guidelines on Post-Approval Changes (2025, superseding FC 2014-008 and amendments and FC 2016-017). Classifications follow the Philippine Variation Guidelines v1.0 (22 April 2020), which adopt the ASEAN Variation Guideline plus Philippine-specific codes.
Change categories: MaV (incl. MaV-PH1, MaV-PH2)=Major Variation (Tell & Do) | MiV-PA=Minor Variation: Prior Approval (Tell & Do) | MiV-N (incl. MiV-PH-N)=Minor Variation: Notification (Do & Tell)
Notable differences: Adopts AVG but adds Philippine-specific codes: MaV-PH1 (additional route of administration), MaV-PH2 (Rx→OTC reclassification), and a PH06 catch-all deferring to WHO TRS 993/1011 for changes not in the AVG. Uses the 'Tell & Do' label for prior-approval (MaV/MiV-PA) and 'Do & Tell' for MiV-N, where implementation may precede notification by up to ~12 months. Now governed by the 2025 post-approval-change circular under AO 2024-0013 with abridged/verification reliance review pathways.

Region: ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations): 11 member states
Agency: Drug Administration of Vietnam (DAV), Ministry of Health (MOH)
Framework / governing regulation: Variation of a marketing authorization under Circular No. 12/2025/TT-BYT (issued 16 May 2025, effective 1 July 2025), which replaced Circular 08/2022/TT-BYT (which had replaced 32/2018). Changes are classified in the Circular's appendix as Major Variations (MaV) and Minor Variations (MiV), with minor variations further split into those requiring prior approval and those requiring only notification: conceptually aligned to ASEAN/EU models.
Change categories: MaV=Major Variation | MiV (prior approval)=Minor Variation requiring prior approval | MiV (notification)=Minor Variation requiring notification only
Notable differences: Uses MaV/MiV terminology but embeds classification in a national registration Circular (12/2025) rather than adopting the AVG document verbatim; its minor-variation split (prior approval vs notification) parallels AVG MiV-PA/MiV-N. Notably fast notification clock (~20 working days) but a relatively long 3-month clock for both major and prior-approval minor variations. Framework changed twice in 3 years (32/2018 → 08/2022 → 12/2025), so effective category lists are volatile.

Region: ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations): 11 member states
Agency: Medicines Control Authority / Pharmaceutical Services (Pharmacy Services), Ministry of Health
Framework / governing regulation: Variation to a registered medicinal product administered by the Ministry of Health Pharmaceutical Services (Medicines Control Authority). Brunei registers products via the ASEAN Common Technical Dossier (ACTD/ACTR) and applies the ASEAN Variation Guideline categories (MaV / MiV-PA / MiV-N), with a national 'Guideline on Application for Variation to Registered Medicinal Products'.
Change categories: MaV=Major Variation | MiV-PA=Minor Variation: Prior Approval | MiV-N=Minor Variation: Notification
Notable differences: Small market that implements the ASEAN AVG categories essentially unchanged via MOH Pharmaceutical Services; no material national divergence beyond administrative process (appointment-based submission). Working-day clocks are not prominently published in English.

Region: ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations): 11 member states
Agency: Department of Drugs and Food (DDF), Ministry of Health
Framework / governing regulation: Variation of a registered drug administered by the Ministry of Health Department of Drugs and Food. Cambodia registers pharmaceuticals using the ASEAN Common Technical Dossier (ACTD/ACTR) and applies the ASEAN Variation Guideline classification (MaV / MiV-PA / MiV-N).
Change categories: MaV=Major Variation | MiV-PA=Minor Variation: Prior Approval | MiV-N=Minor Variation: Notification
Notable differences: CLM (Cambodia-Laos-Myanmar) member that adopts the ACTD/ACTR and AVG framework as a reliance-oriented implementer; limited independent national variation guidance and limited English-language publication of category-specific timelines. Reliance on reference-agency/originator approvals is common in practice.

Region: ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations): 11 member states
Agency: Food and Drug Department (FDD), Ministry of Health
Framework / governing regulation: Variation of a registered drug administered by the Ministry of Health Food and Drug Department. Laos registers pharmaceuticals using the ASEAN Common Technical Dossier (ACTD/ACTR) and applies the ASEAN Variation Guideline classification (MaV / MiV-PA / MiV-N).
Change categories: MaV=Major Variation | MiV-PA=Minor Variation: Prior Approval | MiV-N=Minor Variation: Notification
Notable differences: CLM member; adopts the ACTD/ACTR and AVG framework with limited independent national variation guidance and heavy reliance on reference-agency/originator decisions. Category-specific timelines are not transparently published in English.

Region: ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations): 11 member states
Agency: Food and Drug Administration (Myanmar FDA), Ministry of Health
Framework / governing regulation: Variation of a registered drug administered by the Myanmar FDA under the National Drug Law. Myanmar registers pharmaceuticals using the ASEAN Common Technical Dossier (ACTD/ACTR) and applies the ASEAN Variation Guideline classification (MaV / MiV-PA / MiV-N).
Change categories: MaV=Major Variation | MiV-PA=Minor Variation: Prior Approval | MiV-N=Minor Variation: Notification
Notable differences: CLM member; adopts the ACTD/ACTR and AVG framework with limited independent national variation guidance and strong reliance orientation. Category-specific timelines are not transparently published in English; administrative capacity/processing times vary.

Agency: Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA): Drug Sector; GCC framework via Gulf Health Council / GCC-DR
Framework / governing regulation: EU-style variations taxonomy. SFDA 'Guidelines for Variation Requirements' (current v6.3, Mar 2025), aligned to the GCC 'Guidelines for Variation Requirements'. Two families: Minor (Type IA, Type IA_IN, Type IB) and Major (Type II): plus extensions handled as new/line-extension applications.
Change categories: IA=Minor variation Type IA (do-and-tell) | IA_IN=Minor variation Type IA requiring immediate notification (IAIN) | IB=Minor variation Type IB (tell-and-wait, default) | II=Major variation Type II
Notable differences: Closely mirrors the EU IA/IB/II taxonomy but retains the pre-2026 EU structure and adds the SFDA/GCC-specific IA_IN tier; performance targets are expressed as SFDA processing-day targets (~60/120/145 days) rather than EU statutory clocks. Product may also route through the GCC-DR centralized pathway; national SFDA implementation governs local post-approval decisions.

Agency: South African Health Products Regulatory Authority (SAHPRA)
Framework / governing regulation: EU-style variations under SAHPRA 'Guideline for Variations' (SAHPGL-HPA-06, addendum + quality/clinical classification annexures, v7/2025). Type IA (incl. IA immediate), Type IB (default), and Type II (major), with working-day review clocks and a distinct handling of name/scheduling changes.
Change categories: IA=Type IA minor variation (Do-and-Tell) | IB=Type IB minor variation (default / tell-and-wait) | II=Type II major variation (prior approval)
Notable differences: Aligns with the EU IA/IB/II taxonomy but expresses all clocks in WORKING days (47 / 87 / 200 + 30) rather than calendar days, and carves out name/scheduling changes for mandatory prior approval even at the IB tier. SAHPRA has been consolidating its variation classification codes (quality/clinical annexures) in 2025.

Agency: World Health Organization: Prequalification Unit (WHO/PQ; formerly Prequalification of Medicines Programme, WHO/PQP), Expert Committee on Specifications for Pharmaceutical Preparations (ECSPP) for medicines/APIs and Expert Committee on Biological Standardization (ECBS) for biotherapeutics
Framework / governing regulation: WHO guidelines on variations to a prequalified product: a four-tier, risk-based reporting scheme (Annual Notification / Immediate Notification / minor variation / major variation) applied to WHO-prequalified finished pharmaceutical products (FPPs), APIs, vaccines and biotherapeutics. Not a national marketing authorization: WHO-PQ is a UN procurement-eligibility listing, so 'implementation' means updating the prequalified dossier. Applicants who also hold national MAs must additionally comply with each NRA's variation rules.
Change categories: AN=Annual Notification | IN=Immediate Notification | Vmin=Minor variation | Vmaj=Major variation
Notable differences: REGIONAL NORM CONTEXT: WHO-PQ is not a national regulator; it is a UN listing scheme whose variation guideline (TRS 981 Annex 3 for FPP/API; TRS 1011 Annex 3 for biotherapeutics) served as the template many stringent-authority-adjacent NRAs and reliance schemes (e.g., ACTR/AVG, several African NRAs, CARICOM/CRS) later mirrored. FACT: WHO's four risk tiers map onto the jurisdiction-neutral models as AN=do_and_document, IN=notify_at_implementation, Vmin=prior_approval (reduced data), Vmaj=prior_approval (full data): structurally similar to EU/ICH but with only one true prior-approval evaluation grade split by data burden rather than the EU's Type IB/Type II distinction. Distinctive features: (1) IN carries an explicit 30-calendar-day tacit-acceptance window from acknowledgement of receipt; (2) AN is reported within 12 months of (not before) implementation; (3) post-PQ change first-action targets are published as ~45–90 days with an 80% performance goal. ICH Q12 OVERLAY (cross-cutting, ASSUMPTION on WHO adoption depth): ICH Q12 (Step 4, Nov 2019) is a lifecycle framework: Established Conditions (ECs) define what is legally binding and thus what triggers a variation; the Post-Approval Change Management Protocol (PACMP) pre-agrees the data and reporting category for a future change; and the Product Lifecycle Management (PLCM) document catalogues ECs and their reporting categories. Q12 does not itself set filing tiers; it modulates which WHO tier (AN/IN/Vmin/Vmaj) a given change falls into and enables downgrades. WHO is not an ICH regulatory member (it is an ICH Observer), so Q12 tools are influential/reference rather than a binding part of the WHO-PQ variation procedure; adoption into WHO-PQ workflows is partial and evolving. NOTE: because WHO-PQ status is separate from national MAs, holders must file variations both to WHO/PQ (under these tiers) and to each national NRA under that country's own scheme.
